metadata.note: The Beech Creek Railroad (Susquehanna and South Western 1882, Beech Creek, Clearfield and South Western 1883, Beech Creek Railroad 1886), Jersey Shore - Munson - Clearfield, PA, with the Philipsburg Branch, and the branches the New York Central worked as its "Beech Creek District" after leasing the road from 1 Oct 1890. Passenger service began 1 Jul 1884 and ran on the main line at least to 26 Apr 1931 ("until sometime prior to April, 1934"). Most branches are drawn only as single proven years ([ANCHOR]) from John Fowler's station lists; see not_yet_sourced. Research report: research/branches/beech_creek_railroad.txt.

The rest: 6.35 mi B&O-tagged BR&P track Clearfield - Curwensville (NYC trackage rights, expected), 2.5 mi ex-PRR and 1.1 mi untagged track Mill Hall - Beech Creek (approximated), 0.6 mi straight line through Beech Creek borough, 0.9 mi untagged Snow Shoe Rails to Trails near Gorton.
metadata.operator_split: Oct 1 1890 (lease dated 15 Dec 1890, backdated): Beech Creek -> New York Central and Hudson River. Jersey Shore - Viaduct (1884-1890) and Viaduct - Munson (1885-1890) in Beech Creek colour share geometry with the NYC Jersey Shore - Munson feature (1890-1931 [OPEN]). The Philipsburg Branch has only its 1885 Beech Creek anchor; Munson - Clearfield has no confirmed pre-lease year, so it is NYC only. Not splits: BCC&SW -> Beech Creek RR (1886 foreclosure, same road and trains); the 1899 absorption (NYC already ran the trains); Cambria County RR merger 1898; the Clearfield Southern (NYC-operated). Karthaus - Keating was P&E (PRR) until 1901 - only the NYC era is drawn.
omitted: Mahaffey - Dowler Junction - Cherry Tree (ex Pittsburgh and Eastern, report block [5]): 1899 [ANCHOR] exists but the 1899 operator is unresolved (P&E or NYC), so no colour can be assigned. Not drawn.
Dowler Junction - Glen Campbell - Arcadia (ex P&E, block [6]): 1899 [ANCHOR], operator unresolved. Not drawn.
Mahaffey (La Jose) - Westover - Patton, Chest Creek line (block [7]): 1890-1893 listings, operator unresolved (Cambria County RR / Beech Creek / NYC / later PRR). Not drawn.
Cherry Tree and Dixonville (block [12]): no confirmable passenger year; PRR-operated 1911-1923. Not drawn.
Dimeling - Kerrmoor - Curry Run (block [8]) and Carsons Run - Carnwath (block [10]): no passenger year found. Not drawn (not proven freight-only either).
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing drawn for years without passengers. The Feb 1952 Official Guide marks Tables 144 (Clearfield - Keating) and 145 (Williamsport - Clearfield - Cherry Tree) "Freight Service only" and daggers Mill Hall, Beech Creek, Snow Shoe, Philipsburg and Keating Junction - these prove no passengers in 1951 and are not used as end dates. Excluded as mine/freight branches with no passenger evidence: Tunnel Mines branches (Peale), Grassflat Branch, the Winburne / Hawk Run / Philipsburg-area mine runs, the Curwensville and Bower branch, Kerrmoor - Gazzam (built 1885, abandoned 1926; the abandonment is not a passenger end), Rossiter Branch (not researched). Freight afterlife (context only): Snow Shoe - Mill Hall removed 1966; Conrail's last train through Peale 1993; remainder abandoned by 1993 except the R.J. Corman lines around Clearfield.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Not applicable - steam railroad from opening.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] Jersey Shore - Munson end: last confirmed 26 Apr 1931 (PEA); bracket 1931 - before Apr 1934. A Clearfield Progress or Lock Haven Express "last train" story would settle it. A railroad.net thread (t169127, unread, HTTP 403) reportedly says service ended by 1931 except one train to Williamsport and that a 1936 listing showed none - forum hearsay, not used.

[OPEN] Munson - Clearfield end: last confirmed 1925, and the 1890-1925 continuity is an inference from the main-line trains; whether the 1931 trains reached Clearfield is unknown. Fallback if the inference is rejected: 1890-1890 [ANCHOR].
Munson - Clearfield start: track reached Clearfield early 1886 but the first proven passenger year is 1890; no Beech Creek-era feature is drawn west of Munson.
Philipsburg Branch: only the 1885 sleeper; no NYC-era (1890-1951) passenger year confirmed.

[ANCHOR] branches (Clearfield - Mahaffey 1899 and 1925; Clearfield Jct - Boardman 1900; Clearfield Jct - Irvona 1925; Potts Run - Carsons Run 1902; Clearfield - Karthaus 1902): single proven years from Fowler letters. ICC valuation reports for the Beech Creek RR would give "operation began" dates; not consulted.
Karthaus - Keating: 1906 is the last confirmed year; whether SX Tower's 1925 "b" is a passenger stop is unresolved (if so, a 1925 anchor).

Fowler's unlettered stations: most stations on the district carry no letter in the extracted text. If an unlettered station means presence in all keyed timetables (1890/1915/1925), the main line, Philipsburg Branch, Keating branch and Clearfield Jct - Curry Run would gain 1890-1925 confirmation. Convention not confirmed; not used.

Operators unresolved: Pittsburgh and Eastern stretches (Mahaffey - Cherry Tree, Dowler Jct - Arcadia) in 1899; Mahaffey - Patton in 1890-93 and the date it passed to the PRR; Cherry Tree and Dixonville after 1923.
Clearfield Southern completion: 1908 (STK) vs Irvona station 1904 (W2KC) vs Boardman in the 1900 Guide - recorded, not resolved.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout; only "two daily-except-Sunday round trips" (PEA, main line) is sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 58.9 mi against 59.1 mi documented (Fowler section 223: Jersey Shore Junction MP 0.3 to Viaduct MP 59.4). APPROXIMATED LEGS: (1) Mill Hall - Beech Creek (east end of the surviving Beech Creek grade at Bridge Lane), about 3.6 mi drawn on the PARALLEL ex-PRR Bald Eagle Valley track (now Nittany and Bald Eagle; 2.5 mi tagged old_railway_operator=PRR) and 1.1 mi of untagged connecting track at Mill Hall - the Beech Creek's own grade here (Fowler's "Bald Eagle Junction" at MP 14.9) is not mapped in OSM and the two lines ran side by side, so this stretch is another railroad's track standing in for the Beech Creek's. (2) Through Beech Creek borough, a 0.62 mi STRAIGHT LINE between the two surviving pieces of grade. (3) 0.9 mi near Gorton on a Snow Shoe Rails to Trails way that carries no operator tag (the same trail as the NYC-tagged ways either side). Everything else is on NYC-tagged OSM ways. Split from the Viaduct - Munson feature at the Moshannon Creek bridge (OSM way 257739139), taken as Viaduct station. The east end is Jersey Shore Junction; Fowler counts from Jersey Shore (2nd) station 0.3 mi further east on the Fall Brook line, and trains ran on over Fall Brook/Reading track to Williamsport - neither is the Beech Creek's track and neither is drawn. LATER-ALIGNMENT NOTE: the trace follows the alignment as abandoned (1966 Snow Shoe - Mill Hall, 1993 west of Snow Shoe), not checked against 1884 line revisions; the Mill Hall - Beech Creek stretch is a different railroad's alignment (above).

segments.note: Beech Creek, Clearfield and South Western (1884-86) and its foreclosure successor the Beech Creek Railroad (29 Jun 1886 - 30 Sep 1890) - one operating line, one feature. First train reached Beech Creek 15 May 1884; "Regular passenger service between Jersey Shore and Beech Creek began July 1, 1884" (W2K); the Lock Haven Republican of 2 Jul 1884 had "regular accommodation trains" running from near Peale to Jersey Shore daily (PEA); the 2 Feb 1885 timetable shows Nos. 1-4 at Peale (PEA). The Moshannon viaduct opened 11 Nov 1884. Ends at the New York Central and Hudson River lease, dated 15 Dec 1890 and effective (backdated) 1 Oct 1890 (WIKI) - the NYC feature takes over from 1890. Headway is an estimate (two daily-except-Sunday round trips is the only service level sourced, PEA, for the main line).

segments.note: New York Central and Hudson River (lessee from 1 Oct 1890; lease dated 15 Dec 1890, WIKI), later the New York Central, working it as the "Beech Creek District". The Beech Creek company's independent existence ended 1 Jul 1899 (PEA; CCE "absorbed by its parent in 1899") - not an operator change. Dated timetables quoted by PEA: 1894 (Nos. 30, 33, 36, 37 - "a constant until almost the end"), 1902, 1912, 1925, 1929 and 26 Apr 1931, when Nos. 30 and 37 had been dropped and Nos. 33/36 still ran (one round trip, a gas-electric car after Apr 1929). PEA: passenger trains ran "until sometime prior to April, 1934". [OPEN] END: passenger service is confirmed to 1931 by the 26 Apr 1931 timetable. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. The bracket is 1931-1934; the Feb 1952 Official Guide prints Table 145 Williamsport - Clearfield - Cherry Tree as "Freight Service only" (consistent, adds nothing). Freight afterlife (context only): Snow Shoe - Mill Hall removed 1966; Conrail's last train through Peale 1993. Headway is an estimate (two daily-except-Sunday round trips is the only service level sourced, PEA, for the main line).

segments.note: New York Central (lessee from 1 Oct 1890). Track reached Clearfield early in 1886 (PEA), but the first CONFIRMED passenger year is 1890 (Allport in the 1890 Official Guide, Fowler 223), so no pre-lease Beech Creek feature is drawn here. 1925: Clearfield was a passenger point, because 1925 local-timetable stations hang off it on the Irvona and Mahaffey lines (Fowler 226, 228). Continuity 1890-1925 is an INFERENCE: the main-line trains of the Jersey Shore - Munson feature (two round trips with constant numbers 1894-1931) had to terminate west of Peale, and Clearfield is the only plausible terminal - but no source read says so in terms. If that inference is not accepted, the fallback is 1890-1890 [ANCHOR] (research report block [2]). [OPEN] END: 1925 is the last CONFIRMED year. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Whether the 1931 trains ran through to Clearfield or turned short (e.g. at Philipsburg) is unresolved. Headway is an estimate (two daily-except-Sunday round trips is the only service level sourced, PEA, for the main line).
